To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of PPARα/ γ agonism and ACE inhibition were limited in the BTBR ob/ob mouse, a model of diabetic kidney disease, and that the model shows some, but not all, features of human diabetic nephropaty.

1) BTBRob/ ob mice develop progressive albuminuria with morphological features similar to human DN; 2) glomerular hyper‐filtration is present, but not affected by treatment with AZD6610 or enalapril; 3) AZD6610, a dual PPARα and γ agonist, reduces albuminuria and mesangial matrix expansion in the kidneys of diabetic BTBRob/obs, but does not prevent podocyte loss,
the leptin‐deficent BTBRob/Ob mouse develops progressive albumuria and morphological changes in the kidney that resemble human diabetic nephropthy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the pathogenesis and progression of renal injury in the BTBR ob/ob mouse.
the effects of dual PPA α/γ agonism on the development of diabetic nephropathy in the BTBR ob/ob mouse.
the development of new therapies for the treatment of diabetic nephropathy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BTBR mouse is a useful model for the study of diabetic nephropathy, but the effects of ACE inhibition and/or PPARα/β agonism in this model do not fully reflect the clinical situation.
the effects of PPARα/β agonism compared with angiotensin II type 1 receptor antagonism on renal function in the BTBR ob/ob mouse model is limited.
PPARα/β agonism is unlikely to be of benefit in diabetic nephropathy and ACE inhibition has limited effects on the progression of renal injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dual PPAR agonist AZD-6610 did not provide renal protection in BTBRob mice, and this was not due to lack of metabolic improvement.
this model does not provide the opportunity to investigate the renoprotective effects of dual PPAα/γ agonists, as the renal injury in this mouse is not responsive to either treatment.
the effects of PPARα/β dual agonism in BTBRob ob mice are limited, and the effect of PPARα agonism alone is not clear.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BTBR mouse model of DN is a poor model for the evaluation of new drugs.
this mouse model is not a good model for testing the renoprotective effects of ACE inhibition, PPARα/β agonists, or other antidiabetic drugs.
this model may not be suitable for testing the renoprotective effects of antidiabetic agents.
